title: Micro-lab velocity pad — Zuri
content:
Purpose: tiny, single-file velocity tracker for short spikes of runs. Use this to capture quick before/after numbers, hypothesis, and one-line next steps.

TABLE (CSV-style) - quick to paste into sheets if needed:
RUN_ID,DATE,MODEL,SEQ_LEN,BATCH,QUANT,KV_CACHE,MEASURE_LAT_MS_PER_REQ,THRPT_TOK_PER_SEC,EST_COST_PER_1K_TOK_USD,NOTES
R-260212-1,2026-02-12,redwood-7b,128,8,int8,enabled,42,312,0.12,baseline cold start -> prefix cache warmed
R-260215-2,2026-02-15,redwood-7b,512,4,float16,disabled,120,220,0.18,tail latency spikes under load; suspect scheduling + NVLink contention
R-260222-3,2026-02-22,redwood-3b,256,16,int8,enabled,28,450,0.08,good for throughput-oriented endpoints; quality ok on small eval set
R-260302-4,2026-03-02,redwood-7b,256,8,int8,enabled,36,360,0.11,small batch, enabled prefetch -> reduced stall
R-260307-5,2026-03-07,redwood-13b,128,2,float16,disabled,85,150,0.28,experiment: quantization needed, failed with degradation in perplexity

Quick heuristics / rules of thumb:
- If seq_len <= 128 and batch >= 8 -> prefer int8 + kv-cache -> latency ~30-50ms on p4-like nodes.
- For bursty tail with seq_len >256, check kernel switch logs + CPU-side queueing first.
- Cost est: cost_per_1k = tokens/1000 * unit_rate. (Using quick unit_rate: $0.12 per 1k for redwood-7b int8 baseline)

Priorities / next actions (one-line):
- [P0] Add a synthetic micro-burst test to reproduce R-260215-2 tail spikes (owner: Arun)
- [P1] Try prefetch + smaller batch on redwood-13b to measure latency recovery (owner: Zuri)
- [P2] Add a tiny eval set (20 prompts) to catch quantization regressions before larger runs (owner: Maya)

Notes to self (choppy):
- keep samples small: fast iteration wins here. 20-run runs are enough to triage most perf regressions.
- copy the CSV header into new experiment file, increment run id YYYYMMDD-ish.
- when trying new kernel path, clear kv-cache and run 2 warmup requests.

Observations from recent runs:
- R-260302-4 shows prefetching reduces stall time by ~10ms on median but doesn't help 99th when NVLink saturated.
- R-260307-5 quantization on 13b needs per-layer calibration; float16 still safer for now.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is scheduler batching policy (auto-batch window) scaling linearly with small batch sizes? check scheduler metrics (prometheus: infer_scheduler_batch_window_seconds).
- Can we get a cheap half-day slot on a p4d-like to reproduce cross-GPU contention? (ask infra)

Copy-paste checklist before a run (mini):
- [ ] update run id and date in header
- [ ] set random seed and note it in NOTES
- [ ] clear kv-cache or note warm/cold state
- [ ] attach run logs link to linked_artifacts (PR/issue)
- [ ] snapshot model commit sha in NOTES

Quick links and anchors:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123
- Jira: INF-784 (burst latency investigation)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01A23B45/p1678901234567

End tiny pad. Keep this super ephemeral — paste into a proper sheet if trending or becoming a reproducible benchmark.
